newsitem.title: USA: Dimon to acquire tobacco dealer.
newsitem.headline: Dimon to acquire tobacco dealer.

text.p: Dimon Inc said Friday it has signed a definitive agreement to acquire Intabex Holdings Worldwide SA for cash, stock and debt.
Dimon Chairman and Chief Executive Claude Owen said in a statement that the deal is expected to increase the company's earnings per share.

"While we are generally reluctant to use equity in an acquisition, we believe that the significant and immediate benefits from this transaction will cause earnings per share to increase rather than being dilutive," Owen said.

Under the deal, Dimon will acquire Intabex, a leaf tobacco dealer with about $700 million in annual sales, for two million shares of Dimon common stock, $140 million in 10-year, 6.25 percent subordinated debentures convertible into 4.866 million Dimon shares at $28.77 per share, and $79.25 million in cash.
Intabex is a privately owned Luxembourg holding company. It owns and operates leaf tobacco buying, processing and exporting operations in principal tobacco markets around the world.
In addition, through an affiliated company in Zimbabwe whose tobacco interests Dimon is acquiring separately, Intabex supplies Zimbabwean and other African grown tobacco to the cigarette industry.
Dimon said the acquisition is expected to be completed on April 1.
